official.description_text:
Postdoc in Wireless network and Integrated sensing and communication
Login and apply
KTH Royal Institute of Technology, School of Electrical Engineering and Computer Science
We invite applications for a Postdoctoral Researcher position in the Communication Systems Division at KTH. The position is connected to the large European research initiative RAI-6Green and the Swedish Wireless Innovation Network center SWE-WIN, which aim to advance resilient, robust, and energy-efficient wireless networks capable of supporting emerging services. The research focuses on resource management and orchestration, while leveraging new technologies such as integrated sensing and communication (ISAC). These initiatives bring together leading academic, industrial, and public-sector partners to develop innovative solutions for future communication networks and sensing-enabled services.
Job description
The successful candidate will contribute to research on energy-efficient network design, optimization, and orchestration across different network components, as well as to the development of sensing algorithms and ISAC solutions. The postdoctoral researcher will also play an active role in coordinating research activities within the group, leading collaborative tasks in national and international research projects, publishing results in leading journals and conferences, and supervising MSc students and co-supervising PhD students.
The research will be conducted in a collaborative and multidisciplinary environment, with close interaction with major industrial and research partners (e.g., Ericsson, Tele2, RISE,..)  and other European companies and research institutions. The position offers excellent opportunities to conduct high-impact research, contribute to experimental demonstrators and standardization activities, and further develop a strong professional network across both academia and industry.
Qualifications
Requirements
A doctoral degree or an equivalent foreign degree. This eligibility requirement must be met no later than the time the employment decision is made.
Applicants should hold a PhD in Electrical Engineering, Computer Science, or a closely related field.
Good collaboration skills who can work independently.
A strong research record in wireless communications, networking, or optimization.
Applicants are expected to have a strong background in at least one of the following areas:
Integrated sensing and communication Cell-free massive MIMO
beamforming, and MIMO algorithms
Joint optimization of communication and computing resources
Preferred qualifications
A doctoral degree or an equivalent foreign degree, obtained within the last three years prior to the application deadline
Experience with simulation frameworks, system-level performance evaluation, or machine learning, is highly valued.
Demonstrated ability to work independently as well as collaboratively in multidisciplinary and international environments.
Strong communication and writing skills in English, as it is required in the daily work
Experience in mentoring MSc or PhD students is meritorious.
For KTH and the research group, awareness of diversity and equal opportunity issues, with specific focus on gender equality are important.
Great emphasis will be placed on personal skills.
Join us at KTH
KTH shapes the future through education, research and innovation. As a leading international technical university, we play an active role in advancing the transition towards a sustainable society. At KTH, you have the opportunity to grow and develop in a creative and dynamic environment, with good working conditions and attractive benefits. Equality, diversity and equal opportunities are essential to quality and form an integral part of KTH’s core values as a university and public authority.
Learn more about our benefits and what it's like to work and grow at KTH.

To apply for the position
Log into KTH's recruitment system to apply for this position. You are responsible for ensuring that your application is complete according to the instructions in the ad.
The application must include:
CV including relevant professional experience and knowledge.
Copy of diplomas and grades from your previous university studies. Translations into English or Swedish if the original documents have not been issued in any of these languages.
Brief account of why you want to conduct research, your academic interests and how they relate to your previous studies and future goals. Maximally two pages long.
Your complete application must be received at KTH no later than the last day of application, midnight CET/CEST (Central European Time/Central European Summer Time).
About the employment
The position offered is for, at the most, two years.

ai.summary: Postdoctoral position in wireless communications and integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) at KTH, focused on energy-efficient network design, resource optimization, sensing algorithm development, and collaboration with industry partners (Ericsson, Tele2, RISE). Involves simulation, algorithm development, and coordination of research projects.

thematic_fit.rationale: Minimal thematic overlap. Position is in wireless communication systems, ISAC, network optimization, and signal processing. Researcher's profile is human-centred XR, collaborative immersive systems, spatial learning, and wayfinding. While 'sensing' appears in both contexts, the position's sensing is about electromagnetic radar/communication signal recovery, not about human spatial perception, cognitive load, or learning outcomes. No HCI, user experience, or immersive systems component.

methodological_fit.rationale: Weak methodological alignment. Position emphasizes algorithm design, simulation frameworks, system-level performance evaluation, and machine learning for optimization. Researcher has quantitative research and basic statistics skills but demonstrated in user studies context (questionnaires, task performance). The overlap exists (quantitative evaluation, ML interest, optimization framing) but position's signal processing and network algorithm design are not adjacent to user-centred experimental methods. Publication and collaboration models may overlap (strong publication record valued, multidisciplinary teamwork), but research substance is distant.

growth_value.rationale: Limited growth value. Position could strengthen quantitative analysis and ML/simulation skills, which are gaps in researcher's profile (statistics at beginner level, no ML listed). However, these gains would be in service of wireless network optimization, not spatial cognition or immersive learning. Would not close critical gaps for target identity (user study design, immersive system evaluation, collaboration mechanics in XR). Distraction more than investment.

strategic_value.rationale: KTH is in priority geography (Sweden, acceptable institution). Strong industrial partnerships (Ericsson, Tele2, RISE) and connection to European RAI-6Green initiative suggest research stability and visibility. However, supervisor/group (Communication Systems Division, KTH) operates in signals and networks, not HCI or XR. Researcher would be an outsider in a wireless engineering community. Two-year postdoc timeline is reasonable. No clear pathway to strengthening target identity or building XR/HCI network during this period.

eligibility_flags: Researcher has MSc by Research in progress; position requires PhD degree. Eligibility depends on degree conferral by application/interview stage.
Position prefers PhD obtained within last three years; timing must align if MSc defence occurs late 2026.
Preferred qualifications list machine learning and simulation frameworks; researcher has beginner-level Python and no ML experience.
risks: Thematic drift: wireless networks and ISAC are orthogonal to human-centred XR and spatial learning. Position is pure engineering (signals, optimization, algorithms).
Skill gap in core position requirements: researcher lacks signal processing, MIMO algorithms, beamforming, or wireless systems knowledge. Ramp-up would be steep and time-consuming.
Community isolation: KTH Communication Systems Division is not an HCI or XR research group. Two years in this environment would not build target research networks.
Degree timing: must confirm MSc completion by start date.
Security clearance ambiguity: posting mentions Protective Security Act but applicability is unclear. May require investigation.
